# QorTime AI

**Meta models explain and stress-test a video-game referee's result. They never decide it.**

QorTime is video-game integrity verification: anti-cheat plus verified skill for console head-to-head matches, with a
signed match receipt anyone can check. A deterministic referee checks that signed, hash-chained receipt and returns
`VERIFIED`, `PARTIAL`, `SELF-SIGNED` or `FAIL`. **This repo is the AI layer built on top of it during the hackathon**:
Muse Spark explains the result in plain English and re-reads every locked score, Muse Wonder attacks the verifier,
SAM 3.1 shows what the referee saw. The AI never decides a verdict. Its signals can only lower `VERIFIED` to `PARTIAL`,
never raise a status, never fail a match. QorTime is not a coach and gives no play advice.

The verifier and match page are pre-existing; the panels are this repo. |
| 2 | **Offline, from this repo** (no API key, ~2 min) | Run the first block in [Quick start](#quick-start), then `node web/demo-170123.mjs` | Output below |
| 3 | **Red team** | `python -m qortime_ai.redteam` | `Outside attacker: 25 attacks · 0 accepted` (offline, cached Muse Wonder output) |
| 4 | **Evidence Lens** | Open [`examples/170123/seen/hl01-q4-a9-h0.seen.mp4`](examples/170123/seen/hl01-q4-a9-h0.seen.mp4), or `web/demo.html` (bottom panel) via the local server | Overlay labelled "SAM 3.1 · visualization, not a referee input" |
| 5 | **AI can't decide** | `pytest -q tests/test_ai_ruling_signing.py tests/test_score_crosscheck.py` | Passes: deleting or tampering with the AI sidecars never changes the verdict; disagreement only lowers VERIFIED → PARTIAL |

Muse Spark explanation (advisory, signed by the AI advisory key, never a referee key):
STATUS VERIFIED

Not proven: who was holding the controller, that laptop countersignatures were made live, ...

## Where Meta AI is used

All four models are called through the Meta Model API. The verdict always comes from the pre-existing deterministic
verifier; every model output lands in a separate sidecar next to the receipt.

| Meta model | What it does | Where in code | Effect on the verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Muse Spark 1.3** | Writes the plain-English explanation of the referee's result. A deterministic guardrail rejects any text that misstates the status or makes banned claims; the result is signed with a separate AI advisory key | [`qortime_ai/ai_ruling/muse.py`](qortime_ai/ai_ruling/muse.py), [`explainer.py`](qortime_ai/ai_ruling/explainer.py), [`guardrail.py`](qortime_ai/ai_ruling/guardrail.py) | **None.** Fail-closed: no key, error or guardrail hit = no explanation |
| **Muse Spark 1.3** | Second, independent reader of the scorebug at every locked score. On 170123: 2 of 2 checked locked scores agree (third: unsure → unchecked), ~$0.009 for 6 reads | [`qortime_ai/ai_ruling/score_crosscheck.py`](qortime_ai/ai_ruling/score_crosscheck.py) | **Lower only.** Agree = no change; disagree = VERIFIED → PARTIAL; unsure/unavailable = "Muse unchecked", no penalty |
| **Muse Spark 1.3** | Filters Show Your Hands play-start candidates | [`qortime_ai/hands/muse_context.py`](qortime_ai/hands/muse_context.py) | **Remove-only**; Show Your Hands is capped at PARTIAL |
| **Muse Spark 1.3** | Cited captions (Evidence Lens) and red-team explanations: every sentence must cite a field, checked by code and a banned-word filter | [`qortime_ai/seen/build.py`](qortime_ai/seen/build.py), [`qortime_ai/redteam/generate.py`](qortime_ai/redteam/generate.py) | **None** |
| **SAM 3.1** | Video-tracks the scorebug and players for the "What the referee saw" Evidence Lens | [`qortime_ai/seen/sam_video.py`](qortime_ai/seen/sam_video.py) | **None** (visualization, not a referee input) |
| **SAM 3.1** | Tracks the pause-menu highlight for Challenge Echo | [`qortime_ai/echo/video.py`](qortime_ai/echo/video.py) | **Info only**; a mismatch can at most lower VERIFIED → PARTIAL |
| **SAM 3.1** | Boxes the scorebug for viewers | [`qortime_ai/ai_ruling/sam_scorebug.py`](qortime_ai/ai_ruling/sam_scorebug.py) | **None** (info only; never a status signal) |
| **Muse Wonder 1.0** | Red-team attacker: proposes receipt-tampering attacks as structured JSON mutations | [`qortime_ai/redteam/generate.py`](qortime_ai/redteam/generate.py) (one live run, cached in [`fixtures/wonder_attacks.json`](qortime_ai/redteam/fixtures/wonder_attacks.json)) | **None.** Attacks the verifier; never edits it |
| **Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0** | Event-stream ASR of the demo narration; each partial's `audioProcessedMs` times the burned-in captions | [`demo_pipeline/captions/transcribe_stream.py`](demo_pipeline/captions/transcribe_stream.py), [`make_srt.py`](demo_pipeline/captions/make_srt.py) (reproduces `data/vo-v6-captions.srt` byte-for-byte) | n/a (video only) |

Keys come only from the environment (`META_API_KEY`); nothing in this repo contains a key. No other Meta model
(e.g. Muse Image) is used. Model IDs and endpoints: [Models, services and open-source](#models-services-and-open-source-used).

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph PRE["Pre-existing · ConWan30/qortime @ 0e87ec3 · not in this repo"]
    direction LR
    R["Signed match receipt<br/>receipt.v0 · Ed25519"] --> V["Deterministic verifier<br/>verify_receipt · verify.js"] --> S["Status<br/>VERIFIED · PARTIAL<br/>SELF-SIGNED · FAIL"]
  end
  subgraph WEEK["Built this week · this repo · Meta models"]
    direction TB
    E["Explain<br/>Muse Spark 1.3"]
    X["Score cross-check<br/>Muse Spark 1.3"]
    H["Show Your Hands<br/>Muse Spark filter"]
    C["Challenge Echo<br/>SAM 3.1"]
    L["Evidence Lens<br/>SAM 3.1 + Spark captions"]
    E ~~~ X ~~~ H ~~~ C ~~~ L
  end
  W["Red-Team the Referee<br/>Muse Wonder 1.0"] -. "tampered receipts<br/>TEST keys" .-> V
  S --> WEEK
  WEEK --> SC["Advisory sidecars<br/>separate AI key<br/>bound to receipt hash"]
  SC --> G{"Lower-only guard"}
  G -- "agree · info" --> SAME["Status unchanged"]
  G -- "disagree · mismatch" --> PAR["VERIFIED → PARTIAL<br/>at most"]

  classDef pre fill:#11161f,stroke:#7d8796,color:#d7dde6
  classDef week fill:#06262c,stroke:#2ef2ff,color:#e8feff
  classDef out fill:#0d1530,stroke:#4f7cff,color:#e6ecff
  class R,V,S pre
  class E,X,H,C,L,W week
  class SC,G,SAME,PAR out
  style PRE fill:transparent,stroke:#7d8796,stroke-dasharray:4 4
  style WEEK fill:transparent,stroke:#2ef2ff
```

What the AI may do to a status:

| Verifier status | After AI signals | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `VERIFIED` | `VERIFIED` or `PARTIAL` | A Muse Spark score disagreement, a Show Your Hands flag or a Challenge Echo mismatch can lower it, never further |
| `PARTIAL` · `SELF-SIGNED` · `FAIL` | unchanged | The AI never raises a status and never fails a match |
| any | unchanged if the sidecars are deleted or tampered with | Sidecars are checked (signature, allowlist, receipt binding); invalid = ignored. Tests check this |

On match pages and in the Evidence Lens, **gold is used only when the pre-existing verifier returns VERIFIED**.

## Built this week vs pre-existing

### Pre-existing (not in this repo)
Built before kickoff (everything at [`ConWan30/qortime@0e87ec3`](https://github.com/ConWan30/qortime/commit/0e87ec3),
Sun Oct 25 2026, and earlier), plus the whole capture client:
- [ConWan30/qortime](https://github.com/ConWan30/qortime): receipt format `schema/receipt.v0.json` (frozen), Ed25519
  signing over RFC 8785 canonical JSON, **the deterministic verifier and referee this repo explains**
  (`qor_receipt/receipt.py`, `verify/verify.js`), the referee service and official post-hoc review, trusted-referee
  list and revocations, transparency log, the website and match pages (including the public VERIFIED match 170123,
  signed Oct 23 2026).
- [ConWan30/qorcap](https://github.com/ConWan30/qorcap): the Windows capture client (capture-card video hash chain,
  DualSense USB log, pause challenges). No Meta model calls.
- **Brand assets:** the QorTime name, clock mark, colors and hero-banner style are pre-existing (from ConWan30/qortime).
  The hero SVGs in [`docs/readme/`](docs/readme/) were redrawn for this repo in that style.

This repo uses that code only as a **pinned dependency** (`pyproject.toml` → `qor-receipt @ git+…@0e87ec3`) and a
**git-ignored checkout** (`scripts/fetch_upstream.sh` → `upstream/qortime/`, same commit). Nothing from it is committed
here. The only pre-existing data used is the public receipt of match 170123, fetched from that checkout into
`examples/170123/` (git-ignored).

## What the referee saw (SAM 3.1 Evidence Lens) — visualization only
**Built Oct 27 2026, in the event window.** `qortime_ai/seen/` chains the deterministic referee into Meta SAM 3.1 video
tracking on QorCap's three **public** match-170123 highlight clips (12 s each).

- **Box prompt = the referee's own scorebug OCR region.** Scorebug in place on 359/359 and 360/360 frames (hl00, hl01),
  anchor moves ≤ 2 px. hl02: in place on 249/360 frames until 8.3 s, then the game swaps in a "scoring drive" graphic
  and SAM's object leaves the region — shown, not judged.
- **Concept prompt "football player"** only splits the referee's own frame-difference energy into players / HUD / rest
  of screen. Aggregate percentages only, never per-player data, routes, speeds or play quality.
- **`examples/170123/seen.json` (`seen.v0`)** binds everything to the receipt hash. No per-frame masks, no status
  field; `receipt.v0` is unchanged. Muse Spark writes one cited caption per segment.
- **Render:** a holographic lens appears only inside receipt event windows. Aqua by default; gold only for a score lock
  when the pre-existing verifier returns VERIFIED. Corner label: "SAM 3.1 · visualization, not a referee input".

Cost: SAM 3.1 6 × 360 frames ≈ $0.43; Spark captions ≈ $0.05. Full write-up (prompts, numbers, render, CLI):
[`docs/EVIDENCE_LENS.md`](docs/EVIDENCE_LENS.md).

## Challenge Echo (SAM 3.1) — info only, lower-only
**Built Oct 27 2026, during the hackathon week.** During a pause challenge the player presses OPTIONS, enters the D-pad
pattern on the pause menu, then selects Resume. `qortime_ai/echo/` checks that the **video follows the input log**:
every logged D-pad press must be followed by the matching move of the pause-menu highlight.

- **SAM 3.1** tracks the pause-menu highlight box (only the menu-list column, nothing player-identifying). A
  deterministic tracker is the fallback and a cross-check: SAM and the fallback agree on 98–100 % of frames in 9 of 10
  practice windows.
- **Deterministic code** does the press edges, "menu appeared" and the matching. Per press: press-to-pixel latency.
  Per window: directions matched N of M, jitter, menu after OPTIONS.
- **Effect:** `echo.sidecar.json` (`qortime.echo.v0`, integers only; `receipt.v0.json` untouched). `consistent` /
  `partial` / `unscorable` add a note only; `mismatch` can suggest VERIFIED → PARTIAL and nothing else. The live
  referee and its challenge check are not changed.

Practice run (10 pause challenges from one practice game; video and inputs kept private, aggregates in
[`examples/practice-echo/echo.sidecar.json`](examples/practice-echo/echo.sidecar.json)): **8 consistent, 2 partial,
0 mismatch.** Median press-to-pixel per window 0.94–1.70 s, jitter inside a window ≤ 44 ms. Cost ≈ $0.31.
Full write-up (matching rules, clock calibration, the two partial windows, CLI): [`docs/CHALLENGE_ECHO.md`](docs/CHALLENGE_ECHO.md).

## Red-Team the Referee
`python -m qortime_ai.redteam` →

| Attacker | Attacks | Accepted | What it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Outside attacker** (no signing keys) | 25 | **0** | Every tampered receipt is rejected by the unmodified pre-existing verifier |
| **Insider with signing keys** (re-signs with the TEST referee + player keys) | 25 | 12 | Inner checks still stop 13. The 12 accepted are labelled **needs key protection (out of scope for the verifier)**: 6 plain re-signed score edits, 1 benign challenge reorder, 5 reported inner-check gaps in the pre-existing verifier, left unchanged |

Plus 1 pure replay that is byte-identical to an honest receipt, reported separately. Muse Wonder 1.0 proposed 26 attacks
once (forged and re-signed signatures, score and winner edits, splices, dropped and reordered checkpoints, timestamp
shifts, trust-tier upgrades, signal laundering, type confusion, pin tricks); the output is cached so the run is offline
and deterministic. Attacks run on a synthetic match with **freshly generated in-memory TEST keys** — never a real key,
never the live referee, no real match data. Muse Spark then explains results with a field citation in every sentence.
Full write-up: [`docs/RED_TEAM.md`](docs/RED_TEAM.md) · per-attack table: [`examples/redteam/summary.md`](examples/redteam/summary.md).

## Quick start
Requires Python ≥ 3.10, Node ≥ 20, git. **No API key needed for tests or the demo.**
```bash
./scripts/fetch_upstream.sh            # pre-existing qortime @ 0e87ec3 -> upstream/ (git-ignored) + 170123 receipt
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e '.[dev]'                # installs the pinned pre-existing qor-receipt library as a dependency
pytest -q                              # 216 passed, 5 skipped (referee-hook integration tests live upstream)
npm test                               # 7 browser-module test files, 153 checks
node web/demo-170123.mjs               # offline: verdict from verify.js, then the signed Muse files, lower-only
python -m http.server 8000             # from the repo root; then open http://localhost:8000/web/demo.html
```
Counts re-checked Tue Oct 27 2026 (with Challenge Echo). Optional overlay render needs `pip install -e '.[seen]'` and
ffmpeg on PATH. `demo_pipeline/captions/transcribe_stream.py` needs `requests` (`pip install -e '.[captions]'`; also in `[dev]`).

Live Muse Spark explanation (needs a Meta Model API key):
```bash
META_API_KEY=... python -m qortime_ai.ai_ruling examples/170123/receipt.json --no-write \
  --pub b283cffb9279f2f90859268c64ef21861ef7e5d9fc773bdb8061af0e80624889
```
Other paid refresh steps: `python -m qortime_ai.seen.fetch` (SAM; outputs cached outside the repo) and `--spark`;
`META_API_KEY=... python -m qortime_ai.redteam --generate` (≈ $0.10). The production integration (the referee's
background hook and the verifier page at https://qortime.com/verify/) is a small set of edits to pre-existing qortime
files and stays in that repo (see [`PROVENANCE.md`](PROVENANCE.md)).

## Models, services and open-source used
**Meta models** (all called through the Meta Model API, `https://api.meta.ai/v1`, key from `META_API_KEY`):

| Model | Called from | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| Muse Spark 1.3 (`muse-spark-1.3`) | `qortime_ai/ai_ruling/muse.py`, `score_crosscheck.py`, `hands/muse_context.py`, `redteam/generate.py`, `seen/build.py` | `/chat/completions` |
| SAM 3.1 (`sam-3.1`) | `qortime_ai/ai_ruling/sam_scorebug.py`, `qortime_ai/seen/sam_video.py`, `qortime_ai/echo/video.py` | `/responses` |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 (`muse-wonder-1.0`) | `qortime_ai/redteam/generate.py` (one live run; output cached in `fixtures/wonder_attacks.json`) | `/chat/completions` |
| Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0 (`muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`) | `demo_pipeline/captions/transcribe_stream.py` | `/asr/transcribe` |

No other Meta model (e.g. Muse Image) is used.

**Open-source used by this code:** `cryptography`, `numpy`, `opencv-python-headless`, `pillow`, `meta-sam-parser`
(SAM output parsing), `requests` (caption script), and for tests `pytest`, `fastapi`, `httpx`; FFmpeg (frame extraction,
overlay encode, caption silence detection); Node.js ≥ 20 (browser-module tests); DejaVu fonts (overlay text). Pre-existing,
not in this repo: `qor-receipt` from [ConWan30/qortime@0e87ec3](https://github.com/ConWan30/qortime/commit/0e87ec3).

**Used only to make the demo video (not in this repo, never part of the referee):**
- xAI text-to-speech, voice "Rex": narration (AI voice)
- Grok Imagine: AI-generated cold open and phone callback, labelled DRAMATIZATION on screen (the phone screen shows the
  real qortime.com verifier output for match 170123, composited)
- Remotion: animated Meta-models / roadmap / "what this doesn't prove" section; headless Chrome: card stills; FFmpeg + x264: edit and encode
- Sound effects and music: original, synthesized with NumPy for this video. (ElevenLabs sound effects were used only in
  early cuts and were all replaced; none are in the final video.)
- Captions: timed with Muse Voice Transcribe (`demo_pipeline/captions/`; the committed data reproduces the v6 narration
  captions — the final cut's extra beats were timed the same way)

## Honesty rules and limits
- **The verdict comes only from the deterministic verifier.** AI output lives in separate signed sidecars; deleting or
  tampering with them never changes the verdict (tests check this).
- **AI explains, it never decides.** Advisory signals can only lower VERIFIED → PARTIAL; they never raise a status or fail a match.
- **The receipt format is frozen;** new data goes in sidecars.
- **No device-proof overclaims** (banned list in [`qortime_ai/redteam/wording.py`](qortime_ai/redteam/wording.py));
  device status is at most "TPM claimed (unverified)".
- **QorTime does not prove who held the controller and does not catch collusion.**
- **Not a coach.** Anti-cheat and verified skill only; prompts forbid play advice and the guardrail drops it.
- **Measured limits, stated plainly:** on 170123, Show Your Hands press-to-pixel is *not scored* (clips could not be
  aligned); SAM's still-frame scorebug locator found the scorebug on 4 of 6 frames, so it is never a status signal; the
  insider red-team pass found 5 inner-check gaps in the pre-existing verifier, reported and left unchanged.
- **No secrets, raw match footage, raw controller logs, gamertags, OCR weights or held-out game data in this repo.**

Per-module detail: [`qortime_ai/ai_ruling/README.md`](qortime_ai/ai_ruling/README.md) ·
[`qortime_ai/hands/README.md`](qortime_ai/hands/README.md) · [`web/AUTO_PIN.md`](web/AUTO_PIN.md) · [`docs/`](docs/README.md).

`demo_pipeline/README.md`:

```md
# `demo_pipeline/`: demo-video captions (Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0)

> **Built during the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Oct 26 – Nov 4 2026.** Everything in this folder is event work.
> Pre-existing vs built this week: [repo README](../README.md#built-this-week-vs-pre-existing) · [`PROVENANCE.md`](../PROVENANCE.md).

`captions/transcribe_stream.py` streams the narration through Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0; `captions/make_srt.py` uses
each partial's `audioProcessedMs` to time the burned-in captions. The text is the narration script, so ASR mishearings
never reach the screen. The committed data reproduces `captions/data/vo-v6-captions.srt` byte-for-byte. Video only;
never part of the referee.

```bash
pip install -e '.[captions]'
cd demo_pipeline/captions
META_API_KEY=... python transcribe_stream.py NARRATION_24k_mono.wav data/voice-transcribe-stream.json   # step 1, live ASR (paid)
python make_srt.py --stream data/vo-v6-voice-transcribe-stream.json --vo NARRATION.wav --out captions.srt   # step 2
```
The narration WAV is not committed (`*.wav` is git-ignored); step 2 uses it only to calibrate model latency against
the narration's acoustic onsets. Committed data: `captions/data/` (stream, response, build report, SRTs).

```

`demo_pipeline/captions/make_srt.py`:

```py
"""Demo-video captions, step 2 (Meta AI Developer Hackathon, Oct 26 - Nov 4 2026).
TIMING: Meta Muse Voice Transcribe only. TIMING: Muse Voice Transcribe only (event-stream pass, vo-v6-voice-transcribe-stream.json).
TEXT: the narration script as already shown on screen in v5 (same 46 cue splits), so ASR mis-hears ("Core time", "CoreCap") never reach the screen.
Method:
 1. Each streamed `transcript` partial carries the model's audioProcessedMs. A word's time = the audioProcessedMs of the first partial that contains it
    (prefix-aligned to the final speechComplete transcript).
 2. Script words are aligned to the transcript words (difflib); unmatched script words (e.g. "one seven zero one two three" vs "170123") are interpolated
    between their matched neighbours.
 3. Partials arrive after the word is spoken. One constant model latency L is removed. L is calibrated against the narration's own acoustic onsets
    (ffmpeg silencedetect on the VO stem, first word of each sentence), not against the TTS timestamps.
 4. +20.015 s: the VO starts at 20 s in the cut, plus the 15 ms the v4/v5 master sits behind the raw mix (measured by cross-correlation)."""
import argparse, json, re, difflib, subprocess, numpy as np
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--stream", default="data/vo-v6-voice-transcribe-stream.json")
ap.add_argument("--script", default="data/narration-script-cues.srt", help="cue text/splits (the narration script); its timings are only used for the comparison report")
ap.add_argument("--vo", required=True, help="narration stem WAV, for latency calibration by acoustic onsets")
ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/vo-v6-captions.srt")
ap.add_argument("--offset", type=float, default=20.015, help="where the narration starts in the cut, seconds")
A = ap.parse_args()
OFF = A.offset
ev = json.load(open(A.stream))["events"]
parts = [(e["audioProcessedMs"], e["transcript"]) for e in ev if e.get("type") == "transcript"]
final = [e for e in ev if e.get("type") == "speechComplete"][0]["transcript"]
norm = lambda w: re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", w.lower())
F = [norm(w) for w in final.split()]; F = [w for w in F if w]
first = [None] * len(F)
for t, txt in parts:
    P = [w for w in (norm(x) for x in txt.split()) if w]
    sm = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, P, F[:len(P) + 6], autojunk=False)
    for a, b, n in sm.get_matching_blocks():
        for k in range(n):
            if first[b + k] is None: first[b + k] = t
# monotone fill
last = 0
for i in range(len(F)):
    if first[i] is None or first[i] < last: first[i] = last if first[i] is None else max(first[i], last)
    last = first[i]
# script cues from v5
srt = open(A.script).read().strip().split("\n\n")
cues = [b.split("\n", 2)[2].replace("\n", " ") for b in srt]
words = []; owner = []
for ci, c in enumerate(cues):
    for w in c.split():
        words.append(w); owner.append(ci)
S = [norm(w) for w in words]
sm = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, S, F, autojunk=False)
amap = {}
for a, b, n in sm.get_matching_blocks():
    for k in range(n): amap[a + k] = b + k
E_ = np.full(len(S), np.nan)
for i, j in amap.items():
    if S[i]: E_[i] = first[j] / 1000.0
idx = np.where(~np.isnan(E_))[0]
E_ = np.interp(np.arange(len(S)), idx, E_[idx])
# latency calibration vs acoustic onsets of the VO stem
out = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-nostats", "-i", A.vo, "-af", "silencedetect=n=-40dB:d=0.18", "-f", "null", "-"], capture_output=True, text=True).stderr
onsets = np.array([0.16] + [float(x) for x in re.findall(r"silence_end: ([0-9.]+)", out)])
sent_first = [i for i in range(len(words)) if i == 0 or re.search(r"[.:—?!]$", words[i - 1]) or words[i - 1] == "—"]
best = None
for L in np.arange(0.0, 2.5, 0.01):
    err = np.median([np.min(np.abs(onsets - (E_[i] - L))) for i in sent_first])
    if best is None or err < best[1]: best = (round(float(L), 2), float(err))
L = best[0]
T = E_ - L
starts = []; ends = []
for ci in range(len(cues)):
    ws = [i for i in range(len(words)) if owner[i] == ci]
    starts.append(max(0.0, T[ws[0]]))
for ci in range(len(cues)):
    ws = [i for i in range(len(words)) if owner[i] == ci]
    e = T[ws[-1]] + 0.45
    if ci + 1 < len(cues): e = min(e, starts[ci + 1]) if starts[ci + 1] - e < 0.25 else e
    ends.append(max(e, starts[ci] + 0.3))
for ci in range(len(cues) - 1):  # no overlaps
    if ends[ci] > starts[ci + 1]: ends[ci] = starts[ci + 1]
fmt = lambda s: "%02d:%02d:%02d,%03d" % (int(s // 3600), int(s // 60 % 60), int(s % 60), int(round((s % 1) * 1000)) % 1000)
with open(A.out, "w") as f:
    for i, (s, e, c) in enumerate(zip(starts, ends, cues), 1):
        f.write(f"{i}\n{fmt(s + OFF)} --> {fmt(e + OFF)}\n{c}\n\n")
# compare with v5 (TTS-timed) cues for the report only
v5s = []
for b in srt:
    tline = b.split("\n")[1]; h, m, s = tline.split(" --> ")[0].replace(",", ".").split(":"); v5s.append(int(h) * 3600 + int(m) * 60 + float(s))
d = np.array(starts) + OFF - np.array(v5s)
meta = {"latency_s": L, "latency_fit_median_err_s": round(best[1], 3), "partials": len(parts), "asr_words": len(F), "script_words": len(S), "script_words_matched": len(amap),
        "cues": len(cues), "start_shift_vs_v5_s": {"median": round(float(np.median(d)), 3), "mean_abs": round(float(np.abs(d).mean()), 3), "max_abs": round(float(np.abs(d).max()), 3)}}
json.dump(meta, open(A.out.replace(".srt", "-build.json"), "w"), indent=1); print(json.dumps(meta))

```

`demo_pipeline/captions/transcribe_stream.py`:

```py
"""Demo-video captions, step 1: Meta Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0 on the narration stem (event-stream mode).

Every streamed partial transcript carries the model's audioProcessedMs, which step 2 (make_srt.py) uses as caption timing.
Built during the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 26 - Nov 4 2026). Key from env META_API_KEY (never hard-coded, never logged).

  python transcribe_stream.py NARRATION_24k_mono.wav data/voice-transcribe-stream.json
"""
import json, os, sys, time, wave

import requests

KW = ["QorTime", "QorCap", "Muse Spark", "SAM", "Muse Voice Transcribe", "Show Your Hands", "scorebug", "VERIFIED", "PARTIAL", "Madden", "Call of Duty", "Meta"]


def main(wav: str, out_path: str) -> int:
    key = os.environ.get("META_API_KEY") or os.environ.get("MODEL_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        print("set META_API_KEY", file=sys.stderr); return 2
    w = wave.open(wav); sec = w.getnframes() / w.getframerate()
    req = {"model": "muse-voice-transcribe-1.0", "audioEncoding": "WAV", "mode": "ENDPOINTING", "languageBias": ["English"],
           "keywords": KW, "partialMode": "CUMULATIVE", "emitAudioProgress": True}
    events = []
    with open(wav, "rb") as a:
        r = requests.post("https://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/transcribe?sessionId=qortime-demo-captions-stream",
                          headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}", "Accept": "text/event-stream"},
                          files={"request": (None, json.dumps(req), "application/json"), "audio": ("vo.wav", a, "audio/wav")},
                          timeout=600, stream=True)
        print("http", r.status_code)
        for line in r.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
            if line and line.startswith("data:"):
                try: events.append(json.loads(line[5:].strip()))
                except Exception: events.append({"raw": line[:500]})
    out = {"fetched_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"), "audio_s": round(sec, 3), "request": req, "http": r.status_code,
           "accept": "text/event-stream", "events": events}
    json.dump(out, open(out_path, "w"), indent=1)
    print(f"{len(events)} events -> {out_path} (~${sec / 3600 * 0.18:.4f})")
    return 0 if r.status_code == 200 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(*sys.argv[1:3]))

```

[← README](../README.md) · [Docs index](README.md)

# Challenge Echo — SAM 3.1, info only, lower-only

> Built Oct 27 2026, during the hackathon week. A mismatch can at most lower VERIFIED → PARTIAL; nothing else. The live referee and its challenge check are not changed.

**Built Oct 27 2026, during the hackathon week.** During a pause challenge the player presses OPTIONS, enters the
D-pad pattern on the pause menu, then selects Resume. `qortime_ai/echo/` checks that the **video follows the input
log**: every logged D-pad press must be followed by the matching move of the pause-menu highlight.
- **What SAM 3.1 does:** tracks the pause-menu highlight box. Only the menu window is sent, only the menu-list column
  (left 30 % × top 47 % of the frame, nothing player-identifying), at 30 fps; a **box prompt** on the first menu frame
  seeds one object and SAM propagates it forward. The track is the box's centre row.
- **What is deterministic code (not SAM):** press edges from `inputs.jsonl`; finding the highlight box that seeds the
  prompt; "menu appeared" (whole-frame luma goes dark after OPTIONS); the matching. A deterministic tracker (bright
  rows of the highlight box) is the fallback when SAM is off or fails, and a cross-check: on the practice set SAM and
  the fallback agree on 98–100 % of frames in 9 of 10 windows (72 % in the sloppy one, where a sub-menu opens).
- **Matching:** DOWN/UP must move the highlight one row (wrap included) within ±100 ms of the window's common lag;
  LEFT/RIGHT do nothing on this vertical menu, so Echo only checks the highlight held still (counted, marked
  `visible: false`). Per press: press-to-pixel latency in ms. Per window: directions matched N of M, jitter, and
  whether the menu appeared after the OPTIONS press. Latencies are reported against the known 0.5–2.4 s capture/relay gap.
- **Effect:** `echo.sidecar.json` (schema `qortime.echo.v0`, integers only, next to the receipt; `receipt.v0.json` is
  untouched). `consistent` / `partial` / `unscorable` add a note only; `mismatch` can suggest VERIFIED → PARTIAL and
  nothing else (`qortime_ai/echo/sidecar.py`, tests). The browser panel (`web/echo-view.js`) is info-only and never
  changes the status. The live referee and its challenge check are not changed.

Practice run (10 pause challenges from one practice game, video and inputs kept private; aggregates in
`examples/practice-echo/echo.sidecar.json`): **8 consistent, 2 partial, 0 mismatch.** Median press-to-pixel per window
0.94–1.70 s, jitter inside a window ≤ 44 ms. The sloppy window (D-pad DOWN pressed six times, no LEFT/RIGHT/UP) comes out
`partial`, 1/4 directions; its six DOWN presses all line up with six highlight moves. One other window is `partial`
because the private extract has no release reports, so two quick DOWN presses read as one. The offset between the
video and input clocks was calibrated from the OPTIONS → pause-menu latency (see the sidecar's `clock`); absolute
latencies move with that offset, the jitter inside a window does not. The video also showed that the logged bit
8192 is DOWN (not LEFT), as in `hands/track.py`. Cost: SAM 3.1, 1,571 frames ≈ $0.31 including one probe.
```bash
META_API_KEY=... python -m qortime_ai.echo VIDEO inputs.jsonl --video-start-us T0 --pattern LEFT,DOWN,RIGHT,UP \
  --receipt receipt.v0.json --cache /private/cache --ledger spend.jsonl      # --no-sam = deterministic tracker only
```
Tests: `tests/test_echo.py` (synthetic presses, tracks and a drawn synthetic video), `web/echo.test.mjs`.

```

# What the referee saw — SAM 3.1 Evidence Lens

> **Visualization only, not a referee input.** Built Oct 27 2026, during the hackathon week. The referee and receipt it visualizes are pre-existing (QorTime @ `0e87ec3`).

Built Oct 27 2026, in the event window. `qortime_ai/seen/` chains the deterministic referee into Meta SAM 3.1 video
tracking on QorCap's three **public** match-170123 highlight clips (12 s each):
1. **Box prompt = the referee's own scorebug OCR region** (`madden27_standard`, 640×360: 8,340–485,359), forward
   propagation, one object id. Reports, per chain segment, how many frames the scorebug stayed *in place* (≥ 50 % of the
   OCR region inside SAM's mask), how far its anchor edges moved, and any dropouts / swaps. hl00 and hl01: 359/359 and
   360/360 frames in place, anchor moves ≤ 2 px. hl02: in place on 249/360 frames, until 8.3 s (the lock is at 8.0 s); the game then swaps
   in a "scoring drive" graphic and SAM's object leaves the OCR region — shown, not judged.
2. **Concept prompt "football player"** used ONLY to split the referee's own frame-difference energy (as in
   `motion_series`) into players / HUD / rest of screen. Aggregate percentages only — never per-player data, routes,
   speeds or play quality. On these clips most motion energy is camera and field movement (players 0–21 % per segment).
3. **`examples/170123/seen.json` (schema `seen.v0`)**: receipt JCS sha256, segment seqs + segment sha256s from the
   highlight manifest, SAM model and prompt types, summary numbers, Muse Spark captions, and the sha256 of each rendered
   overlay. No per-frame masks or boxes, no status field; receipt.v0 is unchanged. The receipt does not publish which
   segments the motion rule's random draw sampled, so seen.json says these are the chain segments the clips cover.
4. **Muse Spark 1.3** writes one caption per segment citing seen.json / receipt fields in `[brackets]`; the red-team
   citation checker + banned-word filter + a "not a coach" lint run after the model, with a template fallback.
5. **Evidence Lens render** (`python -m qortime_ai.seen … --render DIR`): a holographic box that materializes
   (corner brackets, glow, one scanline sweep, ~300 ms), follows SAM's track, and dissolves (~400 ms) **only inside
   receipt event windows** — the score-lock checkpoint (tag `SCORE READ AWAY 9–HOME 0 · [checkpoints.away[459]]`), the
   lock's segment (`MOTION SEGMENT 448 · players 9% · [signals.motion_permille.away]`) and any challenge window. Aqua by
   default; **gold only for a score lock when the pre-existing verifier returns VERIFIED**. Corner label:
   "SAM 3.1 · visualization, not a referee input". Web: `web/seen-view.js` (canvas lens, reduced-motion = static frame),
   shown at the bottom of `web/demo.html`; tests in `web/seen-view.test.mjs` and `tests/test_seen.py`.
Sample: `examples/170123/seen/` (stills + the 3.2 MB hl01 overlay). Cost: SAM 3.1 6 × 360 frames ≈ $0.43; Spark captions
≈ $0.05. Paid steps: `python -m qortime_ai.seen.fetch` (SAM, outputs cached outside the repo) and `--spark`.

`docs/RED_TEAM.md`:

[← README](../README.md) · [Docs index](README.md)

# Red-Team the Referee — Muse Wonder attacks, the pre-existing verifier judges

> Built Oct 27 2026, during the hackathon week. The verifier under attack (`verify_receipt`, QorTime @ `0e87ec3`) is pre-existing and **unmodified**. Per-attack table: [`examples/redteam/summary.md`](../examples/redteam/summary.md).

`python -m qortime_ai.redteam` → **Outside attacker: 25 attacks · 0 accepted** and
**Insider with signing keys: 25 attacks · 12 accepted** (plus 1 pure replay that is byte-identical to an honest
receipt, reported separately). Muse Wonder 1.0 proposed 26 attacks once (forged / re-signed signatures, score and winner
edits, match-id swap, donor splices, dropped and reordered checkpoints and challenges, timestamp shifts, trust-tier and
key-kind upgrades, signal laundering, type confusion, pin tricks); the output is cached in
`qortime_ai/redteam/fixtures/wonder_attacks.json` so the run is offline and deterministic. Each attack is applied to a
synthetic dual match played through the pre-existing referee service with **freshly generated in-memory TEST keys**
(never a real key, never the live referee, no real match data), then judged by the unmodified pre-existing
`verify_receipt`. An attack counts as accepted only if tampered content comes back VERIFIED.
Muse Spark 1.3 then explains the honest and a tampered result; every sentence must cite the fact field(s) it uses
(`[verdict]`, `[result.home_score]` …), and code rejects missing/unknown citations, numbers, statuses or winners the
cited fields do not support, and overclaim words (the banned list in `qortime_ai/redteam/wording.py`, e.g. "certified", "guaranteed",
"proven cheat-free") in any AI-written text. Output: `examples/redteam/report.json`, `summary.md`.
**Insider pass:** every attack is also re-run with the tampered receipt re-signed by the TEST referee and TEST player
keys (an insider who holds signing keys; checkpoint countersignatures and challenge tokens are not re-forged), so the
inner checks run on their own. They still stop 13 of 25: checkpoint hash chain (seq gap, prev/hash mismatch, time
backwards), timing gaps, winner/score consistency, integer type checks, trust-tier recomputation, missing challenges,
challenges not bound to a live checkpoint, missing motion signals. The 12 accepted are labelled **needs key protection
(out of scope for the verifier)**: 6 are plain re-signed score edits (a key holder can sign anything), 1 is a benign
challenge reorder, and 5 are reported inner-check gaps in the pre-existing verifier, left unchanged here:
`result.final_t_ms` outside the match window (2), challenge `hid_sha256` only format-checked, free-text
`referee.key_kind`, and player pubkeys swappable between roles because checkpoint chains are checked only against the
referee countersignature. Per-attack notes are in `examples/redteam/summary.md`.
Refresh the fixtures (live, ≈ $0.10): `META_API_KEY=... python -m qortime_ai.redteam --generate`.

`docs/readme/make_hero.py`:

```py
"""Generate QorTime AI hero banners (dark/light) in the QorTime brand style. Text is converted to paths."""
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
from fontTools.varLib.instancer import instantiateVariableFont
from fontTools.pens.svgPathPen import SVGPathPen

BS = '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/sand-box/custom/Big Shoulders Display/BigShouldersDisplay[wght].ttf'
JB = '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/sand-box/google/JetBrains Mono/JetBrainsMono-VariableFont_wght.ttf'

def load(p, w):
    f = TTFont(p); return instantiateVariableFont(f, {'wght': w})

FONTS = {'bs': load(BS, 900), 'jb': load(JB, 500), 'jbb': load(JB, 700)}

def text(font, s, x, y, size, fill, track=0.0, anchor='start'):
    f = FONTS[font]; upm = f['head'].unitsPerEm; gs = f.getGlyphSet(); cmap = f.getBestCmap(); hm = f['hmtx']
    sc = size / upm
    width = sum(hm[cmap[ord(c)]][0] * sc + track for c in s) - track
    if anchor == 'middle': x -= width / 2
    elif anchor == 'end': x -= width
    out = []; cx = x
    for c in s:
        g = cmap[ord(c)]
        if c != ' ':
            pen = SVGPathPen(gs); gs[g].draw(pen); d = pen.getCommands()
            if d: out.append(f'<path transform="translate({cx:.2f},{y:.2f}) scale({sc:.6f},{-sc:.6f})" d="{d}" fill="{fill}"/>')
        cx += hm[g][0] * sc + track
    return ''.join(out), width

PAL = {
 'dark': dict(bg='#04050a', g0='#0c2c34', p0='#0a1640', aqua='#2ef2ff', blue='#4f7cff', ink='#f4f7ff', muted='#7d8796',
              node='#061016', strip='#0a1018', hole='#04050a', pillfill='rgba(46,242,255,0.10)', pillstroke='rgba(46,242,255,0.55)',
              pilltext='#a8fbff', dash='rgba(46,242,255,0.55)', mutedash='rgba(125,135,150,0.55)', brk='rgba(125,135,150,0.75)'),
 'light': dict(bg='#f4f6f8', g0='#d9f4f6', p0='#d5e0fb', aqua='#056775', blue='#1d4ed8', ink='#07111c', muted='#6b7480',
              node='#ffffff', strip='#e4e8ee', hole='#f4f6f8', pillfill='rgba(5,103,117,0.08)', pillstroke='rgba(5,103,117,0.55)',
              pilltext='#044f5a', dash='rgba(5,103,117,0.65)', mutedash='rgba(107,116,128,0.55)', brk='rgba(107,116,128,0.8)'),
}

def hero(mode):
    c = PAL[mode]; o = []
    o.append('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1280" height="640" viewBox="0 0 1280 640" role="img">')
    o.append('<title>QorTime AI</title><desc>QorTime AI. Meta Muse explains the referee\'s result; it never decides it. '
             'Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Indie Developer track. Pipeline: receipt and referee (pre-existing), then explain, attack and see (built this week with Meta models).</desc>')
    o.append(f'<defs><radialGradient id="g" cx="0.08" cy="0.0" r="0.9"><stop offset="0" stop-color="{c["g0"]}"/><stop offset="0.62" stop-color="{c["bg"]}"/></radialGradient>'
             f'<radialGradient id="p" cx="1.0" cy="1.1" r="0.6"><stop offset="0" stop-color="{c["p0"]}" stop-opacity="0.85"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="{c["bg"]}" stop-opacity="0"/></radialGradient></defs>')
    o.append(f'<rect width="1280" height="640" fill="{c["bg"]}"/><rect width="1280" height="640" fill="url(#g)"/><rect width="1280" height="640" fill="url(#p)"/><rect width="8" height="640" fill="{c["aqua"]}"/>')
    # clock mark (QorTime brand)
    o.append(f'<g transform="translate(60.0,92.0) scale(4.1500)"><circle cx="32" cy="32" r="27" fill="none" stroke="{c["aqua"]}" stroke-width="5"/>'
             f'<g stroke="{c["aqua"]}" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"><path d="M32 9v5M55 32h-5M32 55v-5M9 32h5"/></g>'
             f'<path d="M32 32V19" stroke="{c["ink"]}" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"/><g><animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate" from="0 32 32" to="360 32 32" dur="16s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>'
             f'<path d="M32 32l17 17" stroke="{c["blue"]}" stroke-width="6" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="32" cy="32" r="5" fill="{c["blue"]}"/></g></g>')
    x0, base = 360.0, 290.0
    s, w1 = text('bs', 'QOR', x0, base, 196, c['ink'], track=6); o.append(s)
    s, w2 = text('bs', 'TIME', x0 + w1 + 10, base, 196, c['blue'], track=6); o.append(s)
    ax = x0 + w1 + 10 + w2 + 26
    # "AI" chip
    s, wa = text('bs', 'AI', 0, 0, 120, c['aqua'], track=4)
    chip_w = wa + 44
    o.append(f'<rect x="{ax:.1f}" y="{base-130:.1f}" width="{chip_w:.1f}" height="130" rx="18" fill="none" stroke="{c["aqua"]}" stroke-width="5"/>')
    s, _ = text('bs', 'AI', ax + 22, base - 20, 120, c['aqua'], track=4); o.append(s)
    # tagline
    s, wt = text('jb', 'MUSE EXPLAINS.  IT NEVER DECIDES.', x0 + 4, base + 62, 34, c['aqua'], track=1.2); o.append(s)
    # pill
    pill = 'META GLOBAL AI DEVELOPER HACKATHON  ·  INDIE TRACK'
    s, wp = text('jb', pill, x0 + 20, base + 120, 24, c['pilltext'], track=0.8)
    o.append(f'<rect x="{x0+2:.1f}" y="{base+90:.1f}" width="{wp+36:.1f}" height="42" rx="21" fill="{c["pillfill"]}" stroke="{c["pillstroke"]}" stroke-width="1.5"/>'); o.append(s)
    # pipeline
    y = 506.0
    xs = [250.0, 410.0, 610.0, 790.0, 970.0]
    labels = ['RECEIPT', 'REFEREE', 'EXPLAIN', 'ATTACK', 'SEE']
    subs = ['signed', 'deterministic', 'Muse Spark', 'Muse Wonder', 'SAM 3.1']
    o.append(f'<line x1="{xs[0]}" y1="{y}" x2="{xs[1]}" y2="{y}" stroke="{c["mutedash"]}" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="4 8"/>')
    o.append(f'<line x1="{xs[1]}" y1="{y}" x2="{xs[4]}" y2="{y}" stroke="{c["dash"]}" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="4 8"/>')
    for i, (x, lab, sub) in enumerate(zip(xs, labels, subs)):
        col = c['muted'] if i < 2 else c['aqua']
        o.append(f'<circle cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="11" fill="{c["node"]}" stroke="{col}" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="3.5" fill="{col}"/>')
        s, _ = text('jbb', lab, x, y + 46, 26, c['ink'] if i >= 2 else c['muted'], track=1.0, anchor='middle'); o.append(s)
        s, _ = text('jb', sub, x, y + 72, 18, col, track=0.3, anchor='middle'); o.append(s)
    # brackets above nodes: pre-existing vs built this week
    def bracket(x1, x2, label, col, tcol):
        yb = y - 34
        o.append(f'<path d="M{x1} {yb+8}V{yb}H{x2}V{yb+8}" fill="none" stroke="{col}" stroke-width="1.5"/>')
        s, _ = text('jb', label, (x1 + x2) / 2, yb - 9, 16, tcol, track=1.2, anchor='middle'); o.append(s)
    bracket(xs[0] - 40, xs[1] + 40, 'PRE-EXISTING', c['brk'], c['muted'])
    bracket(xs[2] - 60, xs[4] + 40, 'BUILT THIS WEEK  ·  META MODELS', c['pillstroke'], c['aqua'])
    vals = ';'.join(f'{x}' for x in xs + [xs[0]])
    o.append(f'<circle cx="{xs[0]}" cy="{y}" r="5.5" fill="{c["blue"]}"><animate attributeName="cx" values="{vals}" dur="7s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></circle>')
    # film strip
    o.append(f'<rect x="0" y="624.0" width="1280" height="26" fill="{c["strip"]}"/>')
    o.append(''.join(f'<circle cx="{18+24*i}" cy="636.0" r="6.5" fill="{c["hole"]}"/>' for i in range(54)))
    o.append('</svg>')
    return ''.join(o)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    import sys
    out = sys.argv[1]
    for m in ('dark', 'light'):
        open(f'{out}/hero-{m}.svg', 'w').write(hero(m))

```

`examples/README.md`:

```md
# `examples/`: published outputs

> **Built during the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Oct 26 – Nov 4 2026.** Everything in this folder is event work.
> Pre-existing vs built this week: [repo README](../README.md#built-this-week-vs-pre-existing) · [`PROVENANCE.md`](../PROVENANCE.md).

| Path | What | Made by |
|---|---|---|
| `170123/ai_ruling.json`, `score_crosscheck.json`, `hands.json` | signed advisory files for the public VERIFIED match 170123 (AI advisory key, bound to the receipt hash) | Muse Spark 1.3 |
| `170123/ai_ruling_170123_{pinned,unpinned}.example.json` | real Muse Spark explanations, pinned (VERIFIED) and unpinned (PARTIAL) | Muse Spark 1.3 |
| `170123/seen.json`, `170123/seen/` | Evidence Lens sidecar, overlay stills and the hl01 overlay video (rendered from QorCap's public 170123 highlight clips) | SAM 3.1, Muse Spark 1.3 |
| `practice-echo/echo.sidecar.json` | Challenge Echo aggregates from a private practice game (video and inputs kept private) | SAM 3.1 |
| `redteam/report.json`, `summary.md` | Red-Team the Referee results | Muse Wonder 1.0, Muse Spark 1.3 |

`170123/receipt.json` is the **pre-existing** public receipt; it is git-ignored and copied here by
`scripts/fetch_upstream.sh`.

```

`qortime_ai/ai_ruling/README.md`:

```md
# `qortime_ai/ai_ruling/`: advisory receipt explainer (Muse Spark)

> **Built during the Meta AI Developer Hackathon, Oct 26 – Nov 4 2026.** Everything in this folder is new hackathon
> work. See the [repo README](../../README.md#built-this-week-vs-pre-existing) and [`PROVENANCE.md`](../../PROVENANCE.md) for pre-existing vs hackathon work.

Takes a QorTime receipt plus the referee/verifier results and writes a short plain-language explanation with
Meta **Muse Spark** (`muse-spark-1.3`, Standard mode, via the Meta Model API).

## Advisory only
- The verdict comes from `qor_receipt.receipt.verify_receipt` (Python) or `verify/verify.js` (browser) — both pre-existing, in upstream qortime, not in this repo. This module
  is handed that result, copies the status, and **never decides, computes, edits or overrides it**.
- It never edits the receipt. `schema/receipt.v0.json` is frozen; output is a sidecar, `ai_ruling.json`
  (`qortime.ai_ruling.v0`, `"affects_verdict": false`, bound by `receipt_sha256`).
- The verdict path (`receipt.py`, `cli.py`, `verify/*.js`) does not import this package (a test checks it).
- Anti-cheat and verified skill only. It is **not coaching**: the prompt forbids gameplay advice and the guardrail
  drops any text that gives it.

## Fail closed
No key, HTTP error, network error, timeout, malformed or empty answer, `finish_reason=length`, or a guardrail hit:
`ok=False`, **no explanation is shown and no sidecar is written**. The verdict is identical in every case.

## Guardrail (deterministic, `guardrail.py`)
The text is dropped if it:
- does not state the verifier's status exactly (VERIFIED / PARTIAL / SELF-SIGNED / FAIL) or names any other status;
- says a non-VERIFIED match "is verified";
- overclaims device proof (the banned words in `qortime_ai/redteam/wording.py`; device keys top out at `tpm_claimed`, which is an unverified claim);
- gives coaching or tips, says "cheat-free" or "guarantee", or claims who was holding the controller;
- is longer than 1,500 characters.

## What the model sees
Only allowlisted facts (`facts_for`): status, game/platform/mode, the claimed result, verifier errors/partials,
referee trust and delegation serial, review check states and details, the `not_proven` list, the controller-input
advisory numbers, and the device-key status capped at `tpm_claimed`. **No** pubkeys, player ids, match ids, device
instance paths or wall-clock times. Device-proof wording in the facts is rewritten to "signed" before it reaches the model.

## Use
```bash
export META_API_KEY=...        # or MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-coded, never logged, never written to the sidecar.
python -m qortime_ai.ai_ruling examples/170123/receipt.json --pub <referee pubkey> --out /tmp/ai_ruling.json
```
```python
from qor_receipt.receipt import verify_receipt
from qortime_ai.ai_ruling import explain
v = verify_receipt(receipt, referee_pub=pub)    # the verdict
res = explain(receipt, v)                       # advisory; res.ok False => show nothing extra
```
Real Muse Spark output for match 170123 (pinned → VERIFIED, unpinned → PARTIAL):
[`examples/170123/ai_ruling_170123_*.example.json`](../../examples/170123/). About 700 prompt / 350–600 completion tokens per call
(~$0.003 at Standard prices).

## Tests
`tests/test_ai_ruling.py` (API mocked, no network): verdict and receipt byte-identical whether the AI succeeds,
errors, returns nothing or trips the guardrail; missing key makes no call; key never in the sidecar, repr, request
body or error text; guardrail cases; no PII in facts; sidecar shape; CLI writes nothing on failure.

## Signing (separate AI advisory key)
`signing.py` signs `ai_ruling.json` with a **separate advisory key** (`key_kind` `qortime-ai-advisory`, allowlist
`advisory_keys.json`, mirrored for the browser in `web/ai_advisory_keys.inc.js`). It is never mistakable for a
referee verdict signature:
- different field (`advisory_signature` + `advisory_key`, never `signature` / `signatures` / `referee`);
- different key kind and allowlist; signing refuses a key on the trusted referee list, and checking rejects an
  advisory key that is a referee key or the receipt's own referee key;
- bound to the receipt by `receipt_jcs_sha256` = SHA-256(JCS(receipt)), the same value in Python and the browser.

`python -m qortime_ai.ai_ruling RECEIPT --pub HEX --sign-key PATH` writes a signed sidecar. The private key stays on
the operator box (never in git).

## Verifier panel
`web/ai-ruling-view.js` shows an **"AI explanation · advisory"** panel (info tone, never gold) only when the
advisory signature, the advisory key allowlist, the receipt binding and the echoed status (must equal what
`verify.js` just computed) all check out. Otherwise nothing is shown. Sources: a dropped `ai_ruling.json`, or the
`ai_ruling.json` next to a same-origin `?receipt=` URL. Live example: match 170123.

## Muse Spark score cross-check (`score_crosscheck.py`, default second score reader, lower-only)
Every locked score gets a second, independent read: Meta Muse Spark 1.3 reads a crop of the scorebug strip
(bottom 80 px of a 1280x720 frame, x 300-980, upscaled 2x) from frames just after the lock, using the same prompt and
JSON schema that scored 111/111 with 0 confident-but-wrong in the box benchmark. Plain code then compares Muse's
numbers with the locked score. Muse never sees the claimed score and never decides anything.
- Per lock: `agree` if any confident read matches; `disagree` only if confident reads mismatch and none agrees;
  otherwise `unchecked`. Unconfident reads (`unsure`) never count.
- Agreement keeps the status. Any disagreement sets `cap: "PARTIAL"`; `apply_cap` can only turn VERIFIED into
  PARTIAL. It never raises a status and never FAILs a match.
- **Muse unavailable** (no key, network/API error, truncated answer): every lock is `unchecked`, the summary says
  "Muse unchecked (local reader only, no penalty)" and the status is exactly what the verifier computed.
- Cost: tracked per match (`cost_micro_usd`, `reads`). `max_reads` (default 12) bounds it; 170123 cost $0.0092
  for 6 reads; the worst case at 12 reads is about $0.03, well under the $0.50/match target.
- Output `score_crosscheck.json` (`qortime.score_crosscheck.v0`, `affects_verdict: "lower_only"`,
  `max_cap: "PARTIAL"`), signed with the AI advisory key and bound by `receipt_jcs_sha256`, like `ai_ruling.json`.
- Verifier page: `web/score-crosscheck-view.js` checks signature, allowlist, binding and cap consistency. A valid
  sidecar is applied through `web/lower-only.js`, which only accepts "same status" or "VERIFIED to PARTIAL". An
  invalid or missing sidecar shows "Muse unchecked" and changes nothing. `verify.js` and `verify_receipt` are not
  modified and do not import it.
- **Measured (Oct 26, non-held-out frames only; 021003/125430/084523/193534 and labelled games excluded):**
  benchmark crops 73/73 visible scores agree, 0 confident-but-wrong, 18/18 no-scorebug frames (8 stats-overlay
  traps) unconfident. Module run on public 170123 lock frames + 14 eval frames: 15/15 checked locks agree,
  **0 false drops**, 21 of 26 reads confident, $0.039. A wrong claimed score is caught by any confident read
  (tests simulate it). Some 170123 frames right after a lock are unconfident and stay `unchecked` (no penalty).

CLI: `python -m qortime_ai.ai_ruling.score_crosscheck RECEIPT --clips DIR --sign-key KEY --out score_crosscheck.json`
(key from `META_MODEL_API_KEY`).

## SAM 3.1 scorebug locator (`sam_scorebug.py`, info only, NOT wired in)
Asks Meta SAM 3.1 for a "scoreboard" box on a frame and reports whether it sits where the game's scorebug profile
says (madden27_standard: full-width bottom strip). Output `qortime.sam_scorebug.v0` with `affects_verdict: false`
and no cap. Use: demo visuals and a crop sanity check.
- Highlight clips carry QorCap's burned-in "SCOREBUG LOCK" label top-left; `mask_burn_in` blanks it first,
  otherwise SAM boxes that label instead of the game's scorebug.
- **Measured (Oct 26, public 170123 clip frames, 1280x720, label masked): SAM found the real scorebug on 4 of 6
  legit frames** (both `hl02` frames missed it with "scoreboard"; "score banner" and "scorebug" were no better).
  That is too unreliable for a status signal, so SAM is not used for any status; Muse Spark is the cross-check.

```

`qortime_ai/ai_ruling/__init__.py`:

"""Advisory AI receipt explainer (Meta Muse Spark). Built during the Meta AI Developer Hackathon, Oct 26 - Nov 4 2026.

ADVISORY ONLY. The verdict comes from ``qor_receipt.receipt.verify_receipt`` (or ``verify/verify.js``) and nothing here
can change it. See README.md in this folder.
"""
from qortime_ai.ai_ruling.explainer import FILENAME, SCHEMA, ExplainResult, explain, facts_for
from qortime_ai.ai_ruling.guardrail import check_text
from qortime_ai.ai_ruling.muse import MuseClient, MuseError
from qortime_ai.ai_ruling.signing import check_ruling, receipt_jcs_sha256, sign_ruling

__all__ = ["FILENAME", "SCHEMA", "ExplainResult", "explain", "facts_for", "check_text", "MuseClient", "MuseError", "check_ruling", "receipt_jcs_sha256", "sign_ruling"]

`qortime_ai/ai_ruling/__main__.py`:

```py
"""python -m qortime_ai.ai_ruling RECEIPT [--pub HEX] [--out ai_ruling.json]

Runs the normal verifier, prints its verdict (unchanged), then asks Muse Spark for an advisory explanation.
Key from env META_API_KEY (or MODEL_API_KEY). On any AI failure the verdict is printed alone and no sidecar is written.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from qortime_ai.ai_ruling.explainer import FILENAME, explain
from qortime_ai.ai_ruling.muse import DEFAULT_MODEL, MuseClient
from qor_receipt.receipt import verify_receipt


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m qortime_ai.ai_ruling", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("receipt")
    ap.add_argument("--pub", help="referee pubkey to pin (hex)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help=f"sidecar path (default: {FILENAME} next to the receipt)")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
    ap.add_argument("--no-write", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--sign-key", help="AI ADVISORY key file (never a referee key); signs ai_ruling.json as advisory_signature")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    raw = Path(a.receipt).read_bytes()
    receipt = json.loads(raw)
    v = verify_receipt(receipt, referee_pub=a.pub)
    print(f"verdict (verifier): {v['status']}")
    if v.get("partial"):
        print("partial: " + ", ".join(v["partial"]))
    if v.get("errors"):
        print("errors: " + ", ".join(v["errors"]))
    res = explain(receipt, v, client=MuseClient(model=a.model), receipt_bytes=raw)
    if not res.ok:
        print(f"AI explanation: none ({res.reason}{': ' + ','.join(res.problems) if res.problems else ''}). Verdict unchanged.")
        return 0
    print("\nAI explanation (advisory, does not change the verdict):\n" + res.explanation)
    doc = res.sidecar
    if a.sign_key:
        from qortime_ai.ai_ruling.signing import sign_ruling
        from qor_receipt.keys import FileKey
        doc = sign_ruling(doc, FileKey(Path(a.sign_key)))
    if not a.no_write:
        out = Path(a.out) if a.out else Path(a.receipt).with_name(FILENAME)
        out.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"\nwrote {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```
